what_its_for: Solriamfetol helps you stay awake if you feel very sleepy during the day. It is used for adults who have narcolepsy (a condition that causes sudden, uncontrollable sleepiness) or obstructive sleep apnea (a condition where you stop breathing briefly during sleep and feel very tired during the day, even if you use a CPAP machine). This medicine does NOT treat the cause of your sleep problem — it only helps reduce daytime sleepiness.
how_to_take: Take solriamfetol by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole. Take it in the morning when you first wake up. Do not take it within 9 hours of when you need to go to sleep at night, because it can make it hard to fall asleep. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablet.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. For narcolepsy, the usual starting dose is 75 mg once daily in the morning. For obstructive sleep apnea, the usual starting dose is 37.5 mg once daily in the morning. Your doctor may increase your dose over time if needed. The maximum dose is 150 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if you can still be awake for at least 9 hours after taking it. If there are fewer than 9 hours before your bedtime, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose the following morning. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store solriamfetol at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. This is a controlled substance — store it in a safe place to prevent theft or misuse. Properly dispose of any unused medicine — ask your pharmacist about drug take-back programs.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking this medicine in the afternoon or evening because it can cause insomnia (trouble sleeping at night). Do not drink alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may increase side effects. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you — even though it is meant to help you stay awake, everyone reacts differently. Avoid taking other stimulant medicines unless your doctor approves. Do not take monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs) while taking this medicine or within 14 days of stopping an MAOI, as this can cause a dangerous reaction.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you experience: chest pain or a fast or irregular heartbeat; shortness of breath; signs of high blood pressure such as severe headache, blurred vision, or pounding in your chest; feelings of extreme agitation, aggression, or unusual changes in behavior or mood; new or worsening mental health symptoms such as hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), paranoia, or depression; signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing. Also call your doctor if your sleepiness does not improve, or if you notice any new or bothersome side effects.
when_it_works: Solriamfetol starts working within about 1 hour of taking it. Most people notice improved wakefulness on the first day they take it. However, it may take a few days to a couple of weeks to find the right dose that works best for you.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and over): Use with caution. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose because you may be more sensitive to side effects. Kidney problems: If you have kidney disease, your doctor will likely prescribe a lower dose and monitor you more closely. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. It is not known if this medicine is safe during pregnancy or passes into breast milk. Heart problems or high blood pressure: Tell your doctor about any heart or blood pressure conditions before starting this medicine, as solriamfetol can raise heart rate and blood pressure. History of substance use disorder: Tell your doctor if you have ever had problems with drug or alcohol misuse, as this medicine is a controlled substance with potential for misuse.
